findings.problem: Zod issue paths matching inherited Object properties caused .push failures; unknown Prisma codes matching inherited properties produced envelopes with missing status/message.
findings.change: Use a prototype-free field accumulator and own-property-only Prisma lookup. Preserve repeated messages, nested/root path convention, known database mappings and generic server redaction.
findings.limit: Synthetic reserved-field and Prisma-code reproducers. No claim of Object.prototype mutation, client-controlled Prisma codes or a demonstrated real endpoint exploit.

findings.problem: Canonical DomainValidationError.field was discarded by the generic HTTP serializer.
findings.change: Expose nonempty canonical domain fields as details[field]=[message] only for client errors. Keep existing public message/code; do not copy arbitrary error fields or server-error metadata.
findings.compatibility: Additive optional details field, matching the existing error envelope and API-client detail contract. No DTO, status or message changes.

findings.problem: Async Fastify validation hooks accepted general Zod schemas but used synchronous parse; async refinements threw instead of validating. Three hooks and command/query failure responses duplicated logic.
findings.change: One shared parseAsync hook selected by body/query/params; preserve parsed output replacement, 400 envelopes and propagation of non-validation exceptions. One private command/query failure mapper retains log labels/status/redaction/detail behavior.
findings.limit: No current async refinement caller found. This extends helper capability rather than repairing a demonstrated existing endpoint. JSON Schema remains a structural approximation; documentation now states this explicitly.

review.supporting_reads: Existing core-error HTTP, CQRS-result HTTP and shared-foundation suites; canonical domain and command/query/result-error definitions; shared pagination schema; helper/client wire contracts. Static validation/schema/helper callers traced, with representative newsletter route/schema/validator, checkout schema/controller and webhook unauthorized usage inspected. This is not every owning module or endpoint review.
review.preserved: Known Prisma P2002=409, P2025=404, P2003=400; existing sanitized Prisma validation error=400; default client result failure=400; server message/details redaction; query null=>404 only when a not-found message is supplied, otherwise payload-free acknowledgement; false/zero payloads and 204 empty responses; existing success/error/action/pagination schema shapes.
review.deduplication: Body/query/params use one validation implementation. Command/query failed results use one private response implementation, retaining separate log labels. Error plugin and ResponseHelper.error already share serializeError; their logging responsibilities remain.

verification.coverage_scope: Five exact targets only: 70 lines, 74 statements, 27 functions and 80 branches at 100%. No whole-backend or per-endpoint coverage claim.
verification.cases: Prototype-named/repeated/nested/root issues; known/unmapped Prisma errors; unexpected ordinary thrown values and client defaults; canonical domain field transport through both helper/plugin with response schemas; three hooks normalizing/stripping input, validation failures stopping handlers, programming failures propagating, async refinements; representative generated schema with preValidation/preHandler/default/coercion paths; created/action/data/page/204/error serializers; default/client/server command/query failures, absent query results and zero payload; convenience helpers and plugin not-found.

open_followups.scope: Every route still needs actual schema/hook/DTO/serializer/authorization and database-backed behavior verification. Generated JSON Schema omits custom refinement semantics and may see transformed input or AJV-coerced/stripped input depending on hook ordering. Representative schemas do not certify every conversion.

Generic unauthorized/result/error helpers do not select an authentication challenge. Checkout bearer and webhook-signature callers have different mechanisms; determine scheme/status/challenge in the owning route/module review. Prior required-auth middleware challenge fix is retained.

PrismaClientValidationError retains current sanitized 400 behavior; review owning persistence boundaries before reclassifying. Generic fallback and unknown exception objects with hostile getters/proxies, log-field redaction and global not-found reflected URL policy require further hardening review. Ordinary error redaction is verified here; arbitrary hostile object safety is not certified.

limits: No live SQL, provider or full application bootstrap executed. Prisma exception instances are constructed synthetic fixtures; there is no database-operation proof.
Targeted 100% coverage does not close endpoint parity, operational logging, arbitrary untrusted exception objects or owning authentication policies. P01 remains open.
Only response-schema factories and new fixture close at current hashes. Error serializer, validation, response helper and error plugin remain open for listed policy/integration gates.
